step1_figure.circuit_type: Common-Source Amplifier with Current-Source Load (Class A)
step1_figure.description: A common-source amplifier using NMOS transistor M1 as the transconductance stage and PMOS transistor M2 as the active current-source load biased by the reference circuit (Figure 20.43). A large feedback resistor (1 GΩ) and AC-coupling network are used to bias the high-gain amplifier in its high-impedance active region.

equation.explanation: The gain is the transconductance of M1 multiplied by the parallel output resistance looking into the drains of M1 and M2.
equation.assumptions: Both M1 and M2 operate in saturation (Class A).

sky130_expected.calculation: For I_D = 20 uA, (W/L)_1 = 10u/1u, mu_n*Cox = 270 uA/V^2: V_ov = sqrt(2*20u/(270u*10)) ≈ 0.122 V; g_m1 = 2*I_D/V_ov ≈ 329 uA/V. Output resistances: r_o1 = 1/(lambda_n*I_D) = 1/(0.1*20u) = 500 kOhm; r_o2 = 1/(lambda_p*I_D) = 500 kOhm; R_o = r_o1 || r_o2 = 250 kOhm. |A_v| = 329 uA/V * 250 kOhm ≈ 82.3 V/V ≈ 38.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard single-stage current-source loaded CS amplifier provides moderate gain of ~35-42 dB in 130nm CMOS.

quiescent_current.description: DC bias current through the amplifier stage (M1 and M2)

equation.explanation: Set by the bias circuit (Fig. 20.43) mirrored through PMOS M2.
equation.assumptions: M2 gate biased at Vbias1 from Table 9.1 operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: The wide-swing bias generator mirror sets the nominal branch current to ~20 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard Baker textbook operating current for long-channel analog cells.

output_resistance.description: Small-signal output resistance at Vout node

equation.explanation: Drain resistance of NMOS M1 in parallel with drain resistance of current source M2.
equation.assumptions: Channel-length modulation dominates small-signal output impedance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Channel length of 1 um in 1.8V transistors gives lambda around 0.08 to 0.12 V^-1.

input_pole_frequency.description: Dominant input pole frequency due to source resistance and Miller multiplication

equation.explanation: Input RC time constant where the feedback capacitance Cgd1 is enlarged by Miller multiplication.
equation.assumptions: Rs = 100 kOhm as specified in the netlist.

sky130_expected.calculation: With C_gs1 ≈ 25 fF, C_gd1 ≈ 2 fF, |A_v| ≈ 82: C_M,in ≈ 83 * 2 fF = 166 fF. C_in,tot ≈ 191 fF. f_in = 1 / (2 * pi * 100 kOhm * 191 fF) ≈ 8.33 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High source resistance of 100 kOhm paired with Miller capacitance places input pole in MHz range.

equation.explanation: Zero created by feedforward signal through Cgd1 opposing the inverting transconductance gm1.
equation.assumptions: Calculated at very high frequency where Cgd1 shorts output to input.

sky130_expected.reasoning: RHP zero typically occurs around transconductance fT of the driver transistor.

slew_rate.description: Maximum charging rate across load capacitor (positive slew rate)

equation.explanation: When M1 turns off, the constant current from M2 charges the output load capacitance CL.
equation.assumptions: Load capacitor CL = 1 pF as in Fig. 21.18.

sky130_expected.reasoning: 20 uA constant bias current charging 1 pF load capacitance yields 20 V/us.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent power consumption of the amplifier stage

equation.explanation: DC supply voltage multiplied by quiescent amplifier core current.
equation.assumptions: VDD = 1.8 V, core current ID = 20 uA.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = 1.8 V * 20 uA = 36 uW (amplifier branch only).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Nominal 20 uA branch current from 1.8V rail.

step3_testbench.description: ngspice testbench measuring DC operating point (quiescent current, core power), AC characteristics (voltage gain, 3dB bandwidth / input pole, phase, output impedance), and transient slew rate with a 1 pF load capacitor.
